sources.title: Martin Dimnik, The Rus principalities, 1125 to 1246
sources.note: Cambridge History of Russia chapter summary on separate principalities, dynastic succession, and rivalry for Kyiv.

sources.title: Lawrence N. Langer, The Rus principalities under Mongol rule
sources.note: Cambridge History of the Mongol Empire summary on attacks, tribute, basqaqs, church exemption, and khanly charters.

sources.title: Goetz translation of the 1229 Smolensk treaty
sources.note: Scholarly-hosted treaty translation on merchants, debts, portage, wax, metals, and free Dvina passage.

sources.title: Old Rus daily life and culture, full Institute volume
sources.note: Institute of Archaeology RAS volume on household objects, dress, transport, devotional art, writing, and cultural continuity.

sources.title: Cambridge History of Russia, Volume I contents and summaries
sources.note: Volume summary on princely warlords, rival Smolensk and Chernihiv dynasties, and thirteenth-century political structures.

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, Olhovych house
sources.note: Chernihiv dynasty, cohesion, Cuman alliances, competition for Kyiv, and disruption during the Mongol invasion.

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, Batu Khan
sources.note: Campaign chronology, Chernihiv and Kyiv sacks, westward invasion, Volga return, and Golden Horde establishment.

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, Kyiv principality
sources.note: Competing princely houses, destruction in 1240, continued principality, and later political transformation.

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, Chernihiv principality
sources.note: Dynastic ambitions, Kalka, 1239 sack, fragmentation, Bryansk continuity, and later Horde control.

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, Polatsk principality
sources.note: Smolensk influence, thirteenth-century pressure from Livonian and Lithuanian powers, and later annexation.

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, Turiv-Pynsk principality
sources.note: Appanage division, farming, hunting, fishing, beekeeping, routes, Mongol control, and Galicia-Volhynia influence.

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, History of Ukraine
sources.note: Kalka in 1223 and the differentiated sequence of the 1237 to 1241 Mongol campaigns.

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, Mykhailo Vsevolodovych
sources.note: Chernihiv prince, flight after 1239, return, journey to Sarai, execution, and later religious memory.

sources.title: Janet Martin, The Russian lands within the Golden Horde
sources.note: Cambridge synthesis on invasion, persistent principalities, intermarriage, tribute, and diverging regional trajectories.

sources.title: Horace W. Dewey, Russia’s Debt to the Mongols in Suretyship and Collective Responsibility
sources.note: Scholarly discussion of tribute, censuses, surety, collective responsibility, and the limits of describing Mongol rule.

sources.title: Jos Schaeken, 1229 Smolensk treaty edition
sources.note: Scholarly online edition of the Smolensk, Riga, and Gotland commercial treaty and its recensions.

sources.title: German, Latin, and Church Slavonic in the 1229 Smolensk treaty
sources.note: Peer-reviewed linguistic study locating composition in Riga and explaining the treaty multilingual textual history.

sources.title: Institute of Archaeology RAS, Excavations in Smolensk
sources.note: Dense eleventh-to-thirteenth-century estates, log construction, ovens, floors, finds, seals, and a thirteenth-century scabbard tip.

sources.title: Institute of Archaeology RAS, a Rus residence in Smolensk
sources.note: Twelfth and thirteenth-century buildings, pottery, spindle whorls, bracelets, crosses, plinth marks, and a later fire.

sources.title: Krenke and colleagues, Lower Town of Old Rus Smolensk
sources.note: Peer-reviewed reconstruction of settlement, Dnieper terraces, floods, erosion, and thirteenth-century contraction.

sources.title: G. V. Shtykhov, Towns of the Polotsk land, ninth to thirteenth centuries
sources.note: Archaeological monograph on houses, drainage, crops, fishing, crafts, textiles, imported goods, and river trade.

sources.title: Motsia, Zhyhola, and Skorokhod, Chernihiv suburbs research
sources.note: Peer-reviewed excavation report on estates, household equipment, piety, jewelry, amphorae, coins, and scales.

sources.title: Motsia and colleagues, Chernihiv suburbs in 2022
sources.note: Peer-reviewed report on early-thirteenth-century houses, antler working, fires, abandonment, and post-invasion cemetery use.

sources.title: A. Potapova, Healing practices in Rus
sources.note: Institute of Archaeology NAS Ukraine synthesis of medical texts, archaeology, trauma, monastic, professional, women, and folk healing.

sources.title: Ethan Pollock, Older Even Than the Tsar
sources.note: Oxford University Press history of early Rus bathhouses, law, belief, hygiene, pleasure, healing, and danger.

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, Education
sources.note: Carefully qualified evidence for cathedral, church, court education, object inscriptions, and the absence of a uniform school system.

sources.title: Rosanne Gretchen Mulcahy, Canon law in medieval Russia
sources.note: University College London thesis on the Kormchaia, inheritance provisions, children, widows, canon law, and source limits.

sources.title: Makouskaya and Plavinski, A child in the world of the dead
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of child burials, mortality baselines, grave goods, and Christianization in eleventh-to-thirteenth-century Polotsk.

sources.title: UNESCO tentative list, Polotsk churches
sources.note: Polotsk geography, twelfth-century Transfiguration Church, architect, original fabric, frescoes, and layered St Sophia remains.

sources.title: UNESCO enhanced protection list, Savior Cathedral of Chernihiv
sources.note: Official cultural-property record for the eleventh-century cathedral and its Constantinopolitan-linked builders.

sources.title: Gramoty, Smolensk birchbark document 2/3
sources.note: HSE and Institute of Slavic Studies catalogue: private household fragment, 1260 to 1280, transcript and translation.

sources.title: Gramoty, Smolensk birchbark document 9/8
sources.note: HSE and Institute of Slavic Studies catalogue: debt-collection letter around 1200 to 1220 with translation.

sources.title: Gramoty, Mstislavl birchbark document 1
sources.note: HSE and Institute of Slavic Studies catalogue: 1210s business fragment mentioning wheat and four and a half grivnas.

sources.title: Institute of Archaeology RAS, Old Rus daily life and culture
sources.note: Academic synthesis of household objects, utensils, clothes, footwear, transport, music, ornament, writing, and cultural continuity.

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, Belarus
sources.note: Western Rus principalities, trade, Mindaugas, thirteenth-century political shifts, and later Lithuanian expansion.

proposedOverrides.name: Other Rus Principalities
proposedOverrides.summary: Aggregate of distinct Rus principalities; its 1279 Ryazan handoff is cartographic.

batchIdentityNotes: Other Rus Principalities is a generated atlas aggregate, not one sovereign polity.
The one 1200 Polygon contains several distinct principalities and excludes other major Rus polities colored separately.
The 1279 Ryazan replacement and 1300 Golden Horde replacement are coarse atlas seams, not exact historical borders or population endings.
